# Functional trait diversity in marsupials: comparing Australia and the Americas


## 1. Research question and hypothesis

### Research question 

Due to the different environment and the compose of animals in Australia and America, there are different natural resorces. This difference causes the difference niches occupied by marsupials in both regions. The main question of the research is: Is there actually more internal differences in Australian marsupials than American marsupials? What kind of trait the difference is mainly associated with and is this kind of difference depart from the phylogentic null model? 

### Hypothesis 

1. Australian marsupials have more internal differences, measured jointly using diet tpye, foraging stratum and body mass. It is still bigger in the same diet group.

2. This kind of difference depart fron the phylogentic null model.


## 2. Data prepration

### 2.1 read data in
```{r}
# read the data in
raw <- read_tsv("source/MamFuncDat.txt", col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                na = character(), skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
mdd <- read_csv("source/MDD_v2.5_6904species.csv",
                col_types = cols(.default = "c"), na = character())
tree_tax <- read_csv("source/taxonomy_mamPhy_5911species_toPublish.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"), na = character())
source_tree <- read.tree(paste0(
  "Completed_5911sp_topoCons_FBDasZhouEtAl/",
  "MamPhy_BDvr_Completed_5911sp_topoCons_FBDasZhouEtAl_v2_tree0000.tre"
))
normal_name <- function(x) str_trim(str_replace_all(x, "_", " ")) # standerise the scientific names
```

### 2.2 Find marsupials 

```{r}
families <- c(
  "Didelphidae", "Caenolestidae", "Microbiotheriidae", "Dasyuridae",
  "Myrmecobiidae", "Notoryctidae", "Peramelidae", "Thylacomyidae",
  "Phascolarctidae", "Vombatidae", "Burramyidae", "Phalangeridae",
  "Pseudocheiridae", "Petauridae", "Tarsipedidae", "Acrobatidae",
  "Hypsiprymnodontidae", "Potoroidae", "Macropodidae")
mars_raw <- raw %>%mutate(source_row = row_number(), Scientific = normal_name(Scientific)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Scientific), !Scientific %in% c("", "NA"), MSWFamilyLatin %in% families)
nrow(mars_raw)
```
There are `r nrow(mars_raw)` kinds of marsupials in the database found after the first filter.

### 2.3 match taxonomy and phylogeny

In this part, I cleaned the data and standardised species names. I removed missing names and replicated name–ID combinations. Then matched the names with MDD database and the tree.

```{r}
# Keep names that identify exactly one MDD record.
mdd_names <- mdd %>%select(mdd_id = id,
    sciName,
    MSW3_sciName,
    mdd_extinct = extinct,
    diffSinceMSW3,
    countryDistribution,
    continentDistribution)


# 把当前名称和旧名称放进同一个 Scientific 列
mdd_names <- mdd_names %>% pivot_longer(
    c(sciName, MSW3_sciName),
    values_to = "Scientific"
  ) %>%
  select(-name)


mdd_names <- mdd_names %>%
  mutate(Scientific = normal_name(Scientific))

# delete empty value
mdd_names <- filter(
  mdd_names,
  !is.na(Scientific),
  Scientific != "",
  Scientific != "NA")

# When the same name corresponds to the same MDD ID, only one instance is retained
mdd_names <- mdd_names %>%
  distinct(Scientific, mdd_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# caculate how many records have in the same name
mdd_names <- mdd_names %>%
  add_count(Scientific)

# keep the records have only one name
mdd_names <- filter(mdd_names, n == 1) %>%
  select(-n)

head(mdd_names)


# find marsupial in the tree
marsupial_tax <- filter(tree_tax, higher == "Marsupialia",
  Species_Name %in% source_tree$tip.label)

# keep marsupial in the tree and cut the tree
marsupial_source_tree <- keep.tip(
  source_tree,
  marsupial_tax$Species_Name)

# find species did not extinct and in the tree
tree_names <- filter(
  tree_tax,
  extinct. == "0",
  Species_Name %in% marsupial_source_tree$tip.label)

# match tne name and tree tips

tree_names <- tree_names %>%
  mutate(Scientific = normal_name(Species_Name),tree_tip = Species_Name) %>%
  select(Scientific, tree_tip)

head(tree_names)

# match the MDD data with traits data
mars = inner_join(mars_raw, mdd_names,by = "Scientific")

mars <- filter( mars, mdd_extinct == "0", diffSinceMSW3 == "0")
# match the records with the tree
mars <- inner_join( mars,tree_names, by = "Scientific")
```

### 2.4 select regions and traits

```{r}
# define america and diet 

american_families <- c("Didelphidae", "Caenolestidae", "Microbiotheriidae")

diet_columns <- paste0("Diet-", c( "Inv", "Vend", "Vect", "Vfish", "Vunk", "Scav", "Fruit", "Nect", "Seed", "PlantO"))

# seperate regions

mars = mars %>% mutate(australia = str_detect(countryDistribution, "(^|\\|)\\s*Australia\\s*(\\||$)"),

    americas = str_detect(continentDistribution, "(^|\\|)\\s*(North|South) America\\s*(\\||$)" ),

    american_family = MSWFamilyLatin %in% american_families,

    region = case_when(australia & !americas & !american_family ~ "Australia",
      americas & !australia & american_family ~ "Americas" ))

# Convert dietary habits and body weight into numerical values, and calculate the sum of the dietary habit proportions.
mars <- mars %>% mutate(
    across(all_of(c(diet_columns, "BodyMass-Value")), as.numeric))

mars$diet_total <- rowSums(mars[, diet_columns])

# filter good data 

mars <- filter(mars,

  !is.na(region),
  !countryDistribution %in% c("", "NA"),

  `Diet-Certainty` == "ABC",
  `ForStrat-Certainty` == "A",
  `BodyMass-SpecLevel` == "1",

  `ForStrat-Value` %in% c("G", "S", "Ar", "A", "M"),

  is.finite(`BodyMass-Value`),
  `BodyMass-Value` > 0,

  if_all(all_of(diet_columns), ~ between(.x, 0, 100)),

  abs(diet_total - 100) < 1e-8)

# Keep not replicated records

mars <- mars %>% add_count(mdd_id, name = "id_n") %>% add_count(tree_tip, name = "tip_n")

mars <- filter(mars, id_n == 1, tip_n == 1)


# keep useful columes

mars <- mars %>%
  select(
    source_row,
    Scientific,
    tree_tip,
    region,
    `BodyMass-Value`,
    `ForStrat-Value`,
    all_of(diet_columns)
  )

mars

```

### 2.5 define diet types 

```{r}
mars <- mars %>%
  mutate(
    vertebrate_percent = `Diet-Vend` + `Diet-Vect` + `Diet-Vfish` + `Diet-Vunk`,
    plant_percent = `Diet-Fruit` + `Diet-Nect` + `Diet-Seed` + `Diet-PlantO`,
    diet_group = case_when(
      `Diet-Inv` > 50 ~ "Invertebrates",
      vertebrate_percent > 50 ~ "Vertebrates",
      plant_percent > 50 ~ "Plants",
      TRUE ~ "Omnivores"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(source_row, Scientific, tree_tip, region, diet_group,
         `BodyMass-Value`, `ForStrat-Value`)
head(mars)
mars %>% count(diet_group, region)
```

### 2.6 Final data

```{r}
# keep species in the final data in tree

analysis_tree <- keep.tip(
  marsupial_source_tree,
  mars$tree_tip)

# order the data with the tree

tree_order <- match(analysis_tree$tip.label, mars$tree_tip)
mars <- mars[tree_order, ]

# take data of different regions out
mars_australia <- filter(mars, region == "Australia")

mars_americas <- filter(mars,region == "Americas")

count(mars, region)
```

## 4. Tree analysis

### 4.1 Define the diversity statistic

```{r}
gower_summary <- function(dat, include_diet = FALSE) {

  # define log mass and stratum , put them at same weight
  traits <- data.frame(log_mass = log10(dat$`BodyMass-Value`), stratum = factor(dat$`ForStrat-Value`))

  weights <- c(1, 1)


  # when diet is added
  if (include_diet) {traits$diet_group <- factor(dat$diet_group)
    weights <- c(1, 1, 1)}


  # caculate the gower distance between all species
  gower_dist <- cluster::daisy( traits,metric = "gower",weights = weights,warnBin = FALSE )

  D <- as.matrix(gower_dist)


  # find the number of data in different regions
  au <- dat$region == "Australia"
  am <- dat$region == "Americas"

  n_au <- sum(au)
  n_am <- sum(am)


  # caculate the average distance of au
  au_mean <- NA_real_
# make sure there is at least 2 species
  if (n_au >= 2) {
    D_au <- D[au, au, drop = FALSE]
    au_distances <- D_au[lower.tri(D_au)]
    au_mean <- mean(au_distances)
  }


  # am
  am_mean <- NA_real_

  if (n_am >= 2) {
    D_am <- D[am, am, drop = FALSE]
    am_distances <- D_am[lower.tri(D_am)]
    am_mean <- mean(am_distances)
  }


  # return the results
  data.frame(n_Australia = n_au, n_Americas = n_am,mean_Australia = au_mean,mean_Americas = am_mean,  delta = au_mean - am_mean)
}
```

### 5.2 Overall Gower

```{r}
overall_gower <- gower_summary(mars, include_diet = TRUE)
overall_gower
```

### 5.3 Observed gower in same dairy groups


```{r}
group_gower <- bind_rows(
  Invertebrates = gower_summary(filter(mars, diet_group == "Invertebrates")),
  Vertebrates = gower_summary(filter(mars, diet_group == "Vertebrates")),
  Plants = gower_summary(filter(mars, diet_group == "Plants")),
  Omnivores = gower_summary(filter(mars, diet_group == "Omnivores")),
  .id = "group"
)
group_gower

delta_inv <- group_gower$delta[group_gower$group == "Invertebrates"]
delta_ver <- group_gower$delta[group_gower$group == "Vertebrates"]
delta_plant <- group_gower$delta[group_gower$group == "Plants"]
```

### 5.4 Combine observed results

```{r}
(observed_gower <- bind_rows(mutate(overall_gower, group = "Overall"), group_gower) %>% rename(delta_obs = delta))
```

### 5.5 Plot of observed Gower 

```{r}
plot_data <- observed_gower


plot_data$group <- factor(plot_data$group,levels = c("Overall", poster_diets))


plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(higher_region = case_when(
      delta_obs > 0 ~ "Australia",
      delta_obs < 0 ~ "Americas"),
    label_position = if_else(delta_obs >= 0, -0.5, 1.5))


delta_limit <- max(abs(plot_data$delta_obs), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25


(p_gower <- ggplot(plot_data,aes(x = group, y = delta_obs)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_col(aes(fill = higher_region),width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", delta_obs),vjust = label_position ),size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = poster_colours, breaks = c("Australia", "Americas"),  na.translate = FALSE) +

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-delta_limit, delta_limit)  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Differences in functional trait diversity",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Gower difference (Australia − Americas)",
    fill = "Higher mean Gower distance",
    caption = paste(
      "Overall: body mass, foraging stratum and diet.",
      "Within diet groups: body mass and foraging stratum.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +

  poster_theme)


```
